title: Gibberlink
summary:
GibberLink is an acoustic data transmission project, with an open-source client available on GitHub, in which two conversational AI agents switch from speaking to one another in a human-listenable language such as English to their own unique language that consists of a sound-level protocol after confirming they are both AI agents. The project was created by Anton Pidkuiko and Boris Starkov. It won the global top prize at the ElevenLabs Worldwide Hackathon.

GibberLink allows an AI agent to recognize when it is speaking on the phone with another AI agent. Once it realizes this, GibberLink prompts the agents to switch into a more efficient communication protocol called GGWave. GGWave is an open source library of sounds in which each sound represents a small bit of data, letting computers communicate faster and more efficiently than they can by using human speech.

On February 23, 2025, a YouTube video of two independent conversational ElevenLabs AI agents being prompted to chat about booking a hotel received coverage for going viral. In the week since the London hackathon, a video demonstration of GibberLink amassed over 15 million views on X, and was even reposted by YouTube's most followed tech reviewer, Marques Brownlee. The creators emphasize that GibberLink's underlying technology is not new, dating back to the dial-up internet modems of the 1980s. Its use of FSK modulation and Reed-Solomon error correction to generate compact signals, while a good design, falls short of modern advances.

GibberLink enables AI-to-AI conversations that are 80% faster. AI agents communicating via GGWave could reduce computation costs by an order of magnitude or more. The project has been cited as raising questions around AI ethics and oversight, though the creators clarify that such instances are explicitly programmed optimizations, not emergent deception. GibberLink's creators say they are not commercializing the project and have open sourced it on GitHub.
